deep.reconstruction:
This page has no text. It is a working sketch for the construction set out on the previous page (5.1.84) and continued on the next.

Setting, from the previous page:
- X is a compact surface with a topological graph X_1 that decomposes it into cells. The case of interest is when all vertices have even order, i.e. (X, X_1) is a system of pseudo-lines in a topological real projective plane.
- A circle D in X is in 'general position' if it meets X_1 only at points of even order and crosses X_1 transversally there.
- Two such circles are 'isotopic' if one can be deformed into the other through general-position circles, keeping the facets crossed (Φ(D)) fixed.
- There is a 'sweeping' (balayage) of a pseudo-line across an even vertex of X_1. It gives specialisations (pushing D onto the vertex) and generisations (moving it off).
- These transitions are organised into an object \tilde D. It carries a notion of parallel transport along it.

What the drawing seems to show (my reading, not certain):
- Several thin pencil curves (long arcs, nearly straight lines crossing in an X, and a closed oval) form a sample arrangement of pseudo-lines, i.e. the graph X_1, sketched in an affine chart.
- A thicker green curve and a paler yellow curve leave a common point at the lower left and diverge toward the upper right. Each carries small arrowheads, i.e. orientations.
- Small hatch marks sit where the green curve crosses pencil lines. They plausibly mark the even vertices or segments the curve sweeps over.
- The two coloured curves most plausibly depict two positions of a test pseudo-line D, related by a one-parameter family D_t. They share an initial segment and then pass on different sides of the crossings.
- This matches the next page: one-parameter families D_t are cut into segments on which the crossings stay constant, and transport of an orientation along the family is compared with 'parallel transport' of the orientation. The next page asserts these are opposite, a nonorientability or Möbius-type phenomenon, as expected in RP^2.

The broader goal, judging from the next page: the set of general-position pseudo-lines relative to an arrangement, up to isotopy, with sweeping transitions as adjacencies, forms a new cell complex. In it all vertices have order 4, and it is again a real projective plane with a pseudo-line system. This is a kind of 'space of pseudo-lines' or dual arrangement attached to a given one.

ideas.what: Space of pseudo-lines in general position relative to a given pseudo-line arrangement, with adjacencies given by sweeping across vertices; this page illustrates a one-parameter deformation of a test pseudo-line
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (single-element extensions); dual or 'sweep' structures on pseudoline arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folkman–Lawrence (1978) for topological representation; Las Vergnas, Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) and Mnëv–Ziegler for extension spaces; Goodman–Pollack for sweeps and allowable sequences

ideas.what: Comparing transport of an orientation of D along a loop of deformations with a combinatorial 'parallel transport'
ideas.modern_name: Orientation character / monodromy (w_1) on the space of pseudo-lines

missed.claim: The surrounding pages (illustrated here) build a cell complex of pseudo-lines in general position relative to an arrangement, apparently aiming to show it is again a projective plane with all vertices of order 4. This anticipates questions about the topology of extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids, studied later by Sturmfels–Ziegler, Mnëv and others. This page itself only contains a drawing.
